subject: Follow-up: slim-retain pilot & data residency clarifications
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Carl Jensen <carl@medimetrics.ai>, MediMetrics Security <security@medimetrics.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: slim-retain pilot & data residency clarifications

Thanks again for taking the call earlier, Carl — good to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before legal/procurement digs in:

- Goals we heard: 1) zero retention of PII/PHI, 2) short-lived operational logs for debugging, 3) US-only residency for any raw inputs.
- Proposed opt-in pilot: "Slim Retain" — minimal persistence profile to validate accuracy and run a short production spike. Outline (high level):
  * Prompt/input retention: 24 hours (default), with an option to redact flagged PII at ingress (see next step).
  * KV/cache: up to 72 hours for session reconstructions (configurable per-route).
  * Aggregated telemetry: 180 days, strictly aggregated/anonymized for model-quality metrics.
  * Residency: us-east-1 only, customer VPC routing, keys in their KMS.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-slim-retain-2026.pdf — includes config options and a sample canary policy.

Asks / next steps:
1) Carl/security team: can you confirm whether 24h prompt TTL + ingress redaction would meet your legal baseline, or do you need strict 0-retention for all inputs?
2) If 0-retention for PII only is acceptable, please send the security questionnaire (or highlight sections we should prioritize).
3) We can stand up the pilot in a Dedicated/Private lane to meet residency + KMS control — Marcus and Neha are looped to scope the SOW and SLA.

If you want, we can also propose a split-ttl model (redact PII immediately, short cache for non-PII). Happy to convert this to a one-pager for your procurement.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Carl Jensen <carl@medimetrics.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediMetrics Security <security@medimetrics.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 10:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: slim-retain pilot & data residency clarifications

Priyom — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying points from our side after a quick review with security and legal:

- Our baseline: 0-retention for any data elements that can be tied back to an identifiable individual (PII/PHI). That said, we can consider short-lived non-PII operational logs for debugging if they are strictly ephemeral and access-controlled.
- Residency: US-only is required; prefer AWS us-east-1.
- Q: When you say "ingress redaction", do you perform deterministic PII detection and redact on the client-side before it reaches your runtime, or is it a server-side classification step? We need very low false negatives.
- Procurement asks: please fill out the attached security questionnaire and include SOC2 Type II report or an SOC2 letter if available. Also, they asked for a sample DocuSign template and any standard data processing addenda.

I've attached our questionnaire — focus on the sections on data retention and encryption. For the pilot, if you can show a hard guarantee that prompt text that contains PII is never persisted beyond the request window (0-retention for PII), we'll be in much better shape. A short-lived cache for non-PII that auto-evicts (<=72h) is likely acceptable.

We'll loop legal if you can confirm the implementation approach.

Regards,
Carl Jensen
Director, Product
MediMetrics
carl@medimetrics.ai

(Attachment: MediMetrics-Security-Questionnaire-v1.pdf)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Carl Jensen <carl@medimetrics.ai>, MediMetrics Security <security@medimetrics.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: slim-retain pilot & data residency clarifications

Carl — appreciate the fast feedback and the questionnaire. Quick, practical response and an internal ask so we can move the pilot forward.

1) Ingress redaction model: we offer two options; both can be deployed for the pilot in your VPC:
   - Client-side SDK filter (recommended): deterministic regex + ML classifier run in-customer lane before any network egress. That guarantees PII never leaves your environment.
   - Server-side classification + redact: we run a high-recall PII classifier as the first step in the runtime and immediately drop matching tokens. For high-assurance customers we pair this with token-level audit logs that show redaction events (no raw payload persists).

2) Commitment we can make for the pilot:
   - PII/PHI flagged by either method: 0-retention (no storage beyond per-request transient memory).
   - Non-PII operational logs: configurable TTL up to 72 hours, access-limited to ops on a need-to-know basis.
   - Aggregated telemetry for quality: 180 days, aggregated/anonymized, with opt-out for specific hash buckets.

3) Evidence and procurement artifacts: attaching a slim proposal that calls out the pilot config and an evidence checklist. Neha — can you prepare SOC2 summary + a pointer to our compliance folder to attach to this thread? Marcus — can you draft a short SOW that binds the 0-retention-for-PII concession for the pilot and includes a rollback/fallback if we see accuracy regressions?

4) Pilot timing: we can provision a dedicated pilot in us-east-1 within ~10 business days after we sign the pilot SOW and exchange a minimal NDA. Suggested pilot length: 30 days + 30-day extension option.

Carl, if that aligns I will: (a) return the filled questionnaire in 24 hours, (b) attach SOC2 pointer, and (c) share the pilot SOW draft. Once legal confirms the simple 0-retention-for-PII clause, procurement can push DocuSign.

— Priyom
